intent: A tiny candle-knight ward that feels authored at native pixel scale and makes one formation decision readable before and during combat.

renderingStrategy.mode: Godot 2D at 480x270, integer 3x presentation, palette-locked 64x64 character sprites, an authored raster UI kit, bundled pixel typography, and whole-pixel causal combat choreography.
renderingStrategy.feasibility: Build and capture the entire representative encounter in Godot. Keep ImageGen output as source only; segment, normalize, palette-lock, import, and inspect every runtime asset before promotion.

references.label: Generated character source sheet; source only and never a runtime surface
references.prompt: Production source sheet for a low-resolution 2D pixel-art autobattler called WICKWARD: exactly six isolated full-body units in a 3 by 2 sheet—three candle guardians (red shield warden, blue match-wand seer, gold bell healer) and three night moths (round soot moth, narrow violet needle moth, large ash moth). Authentic crisp 16-bit pixel art, limited palette, readable silhouettes, consistent scale and baseline, no text, UI, scenery, shadows, watermark, painterly rendering, gradients, or overlapping cells.

references.label: Generated six-motif ornament atlas; source only and never loaded by the runtime
references.prompt: Production source atlas of exactly six decorative pixel-art UI motifs for Wickward: candle-flame crest, crossed ward-line knot, night-moth sigil, wax-drip edge accent, square brass corner cap, and round brass rivet. One motif per equal cell in a 3 by 2 atlas on flat chroma green, all at the same apparent pixel density and scale, using the existing Wickward palette and crisp 16-bit pixel language. Ornaments only: no complete panels, buttons, frames, health bars, text, characters, scenery, giant ornaments, mismatched pixel densities, gradients, or watermark.

nonnegotiables: Rear, center, and front effects remain readable before battle without a tutorial modal.
Generated and segmented source images never appear directly in the shipping view.
Structural UI uses one deterministic native-grid geometry contract; generated ornament motifs are compiled to final dimensions and placed 1:1 without texture stretching.
Every runtime character uses the same 64x64 pixel grid, 16-color palette, baseline, and nearest-neighbor import.
Combat exposes anticipation, role-specific action, travel, impact, reaction, defeat, and resolution through the real engine-recorded sequence.
Planning, selected, battle, win, and replay states share one visual system.

qualityDimensions.formation_read: The eye moves from slot role to guardian to front-facing threat without hunting.
qualityDimensions.pixel_coherence: Sprites, type, borders, effects, and motion resolve on the same low-resolution grid.
qualityDimensions.authored_specificity: Wax guardians, moth enemies, flame progress pips, and the ward-line vocabulary feel specific to Wickward.
qualityDimensions.combat_feedback: Damage, healing, target travel, health, defeat, victory, and replay remain distinguishable during the short battle.
qualityDimensions.motion_choreography: Each role has a distinct causal phrase, with whole-pixel anticipation, action, impact, reaction, and recovery rather than generic ambient movement.

antiPatterns: raw generated character sheets in runtime
concept art presented as gameplay evidence

views.purpose: Explain the single formation decision and invite a swap.
Confirm which guardian will move next.
Show the formation's automatic causal behavior.
Resolve the encounter and expose immediate replay.
